[[Club Universidad de Chile|Universidad de Chile]] is the defending champion. [[Club Universidad de Chile|Universidad de Chile]] won both the Apertura and the Clausura Championships {{TOC limit|4}} ==Format changes== For the 2012, the [[Asociación Nacional de Fútbol Profesional|ANFP]]'s Council of Club Presidents approved the return to the [[Apertura and Clausura]] format, with playoffs.{{cite web |url=http://www.anfp.cl/detalle_noticia.php?noticia=8846 |title=Consejo de clubes aprobó torneos para el 2011 |language=es |trans-title=Council of clubs approved the tournaments for 2011 |publisher=[[Asociación Nacional de Fútbol Profesional|ANFP]] |date=December 9, 2011 |access-date=December 29, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101212200559/http://anfp.cl/detalle_noticia.php?noticia=8846 |archive-date=2010-12-12 |url-status=dead }} ==Teams== Eighteen teams competed in the Primera División for the 2012 season, sixteen of whom returned from the [[2011 Chilean Primera División season|2011 season]]. [[Santiago Morning]] and [[Ñublense]] were relegated last season after finishing 17th and 18th overall, respectively. There were replaced by [[Deportes Antofagasta|Antofagasta]] and [[C.S.D. Rangers|Rangers]], the 2011 Primera B winner and runner-up, respectively.
